**build-41** (digest `sha256:...041`) is correctly flagged for expiration under rule priority 100 (`tagStatus: any`, `imageCountMoreThan: 10`, action `expire`). With 11 tagged images against a threshold of 10, it's the single excess image — matching the preview's `expiringImageTotalCount: 1`.

No active consumer was found anywhere I could check:
- **ECS** — no clusters, no active task definitions
- **Batch** — 0 active job definitions
- **Lambda** — both functions are `Zip` package type (not container-image based, so irrelevant to this repo)
- **App Runner** — no services
- **EKS** — no clusters

CloudTrail's 30-day window shows exactly one interaction: `PutImage` followed one second later by `BatchGetImage`, both from `ci-push-role/github-run-8812` at `2026-10-20T09:15:00–01Z`. That pairing is the classic push-and-verify pattern from a CI pipeline confirming its own push — not a deployment pull. Nothing else touched this image in the window.

## Evidence tier: Tier 2 — indirect/corroborating

Not Tier 1. `DescribeImages` shows **no `lastRecordedPullTime` field at all** on any of the 11 images, not just an empty/old value — that indicates pull-timestamp tracking isn't enabled on this repository, so the direct ECR telemetry that would normally settle this (a timestamp inside the 30-day pull window) simply doesn't exist to check.

The verdict instead rests on the absence of references across every compute surface that could pull from ECR (ECS, Batch, Lambda, App Runner, EKS) combined with a clean CloudTrail trail showing no post-push `BatchGetImage`/`GetDownloadUrlForLayer` calls. That's solid corroborating evidence, but it's circumstantial — it rules out the consumers I can see, it doesn't produce a positive "last pulled" timestamp.

## Repository rating: Moderate confidence — visibility gap

The lifecycle policy itself is working as designed (right threshold, right image selected). The gap is observability: without pull-timestamp tracking enabled, future expirations on this repo will keep relying on Tier 2 reasoning instead of a direct Tier 1 signal.
